verses.english: Linked Discourses 42.1
1. Chiefs
Fury
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Atha kho caṇḍo gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho caṇḍo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Fury the chief went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacco caṇḍo caṇḍotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some people are regarded as furious,

verses.pali: Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacco sorato soratotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchatī”ti?
verses.english: while others are regarded as gentle?”
“Take someone who hasn’t given up greed.

verses.pali: Rāgassa appahīnattā pare kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ pātukaroti.
verses.english: So they get annoyed by others, and they show it.
They’re regarded as furious.
They haven’t given up hate.

verses.pali: Dosassa appahīnattā pare kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ pātukaroti.
verses.english: So they get annoyed by others, and they show it.
They’re regarded as furious.
They haven’t given up delusion.

verses.pali: Mohassa appahīnattā pare kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ pātukaroti.
verses.english: So they get annoyed by others, and they show it.
They’re regarded as furious.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, gāmaṇi, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena midhekacco caṇḍo caṇḍotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: This is the cause, this is the reason why some people are regarded as furious.

verses.pali: Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekaccassa rāgo pahīno hoti.
verses.english: But take someone who has given up greed.

verses.pali: Rāgassa pahīnattā pare na kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ na pātukaroti.
verses.english: So they don’t get annoyed by others, and don’t show it.
They’re regarded as gentle.
They’ve given up hate.

verses.pali: Dosassa pahīnattā pare na kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ na pātukaroti.
verses.english: So they don’t get annoyed by others, and don’t show it.
They’re regarded as gentle.
They’ve given up delusion.

verses.pali: Mohassa pahīnattā pare na kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ na pātukaroti.
verses.english: So they don’t get annoyed by others, and don’t show it.
They’re regarded as gentle.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, gāmaṇi, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena midhekacco sorato soratotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchatī”ti.
verses.english: This is the cause, this is the reason why some people are regarded as gentle.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, caṇḍo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, Fury the chief said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, sir! Excellent!

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
verses.english: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, the Buddha has made the teaching clear in many ways.

verses.pali: Esāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
verses.english: I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
verses.english: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
